item.title: Meshery Operator, MeshSync, Broker Troubleshooting Guide
item.description:
What is Meshery Operator?

Meshery Operator controls and monitors the lifecycle of components deployed inside Meshery-managed Kubernetes clusters. Learn more about Meshery’s architecture.

This guide offers comprehensive troubleshooting instructions for Meshery Operator and its custom controllers, MeshSync and Broker. Follow the steps outlined in this document to ensure a smooth Meshery deployment.

First, understand the Meshery Operator Deployment Scenarios and the Status of Meshery Operator, MeshSync, and Meshery Broker to identify the deployment model fitting of your environment. Then, follow the guidance under the respective scenario to troubleshoot accordingly.

item.title: Troubleshooting Errors while running Meshery
item.description:
mesheryctl system start

Resources already exist and cannot be imported into the Helm release

Error:

mesheryctl system start : : cannot start Meshery: rendered manifests contain a resource that already exists.
Unable to continue with install: ServiceAccount "meshery-operator" in namespace "meshery" exists and cannot
be imported into the current release: invalid ownership metadata; label validation error: missing key
"app.kubernetes.io/managed-by": must be set to "Helm"; annotation validation error: missing key
"meta.helm.sh/release-name": must be set to "meshery"; annotation validation error: missing key
"meta.helm.sh/release-namespace": must be set to "meshery"

Cause: Meshery resources from an earlier installation are still in the cluster, but Helm does not manage them, so the new Helm release cannot take them over.

item.title: Troubleshooting Extensions for Local Development
item.description:
Use this guide when an extension doesn’t show up in your local Meshery development environment. Meshery extensions integrate in two different ways, and each fails differently, so first find out which kind you have.

Step 1: Find the extension’s repository

Most Meshery extensions are open source, with repositories in the meshery-extensions GitHub organization. Find the repository for the extension you are troubleshooting.

If the repository is public, follow the steps for Loosely-Coupled Extensions.

item.title: Troubleshooting Meshery Installations
item.description:
mesheryctl preflight checks

Before mesheryctl system start and other mesheryctl system commands deploy anything, they check that your environment is ready. For a Kubernetes context, mesheryctl connects to the cluster in your kubeconfig’s current context. To run the same checks yourself, run mesheryctl system check --preflight. See Running system checks.

  • Situation: mesheryctl cannot create a Kubernetes client or query the Kubernetes API.

    Fix: Run kubectl config current-context and kubectl get pods to confirm that your kubeconfig points at a reachable cluster.
